name: What if the repaired texture still looks different after it dries?

mainEntity.name: What if the repaired texture still looks different after it dries?

acceptedAnswer.text: If the repaired area looks slightly different at first, that can be normal until primer and paint are fully dry and the lighting is reviewed from different angles. If the texture still stands out after drying, the finish may need a second blend pass or a larger feathered repair area. In neighborhoods like Centennial, Greenwood Village, and Parker, daylight through large windows can make imperfect matches easier to see, so ask for a final walk-through in normal lighting.
acceptedAnswer.description: Some difference can be normal until everything cures, but a repair should blend in after drying. If it still shows, the texture may need more blending.
